Examples of Support Services include career advice, job placement, childcare, transportation, tools, mentorship, counseling, and other forms of aid.

Formal agreement between two or more parties that specifies how prior learning is recognized, including its transfer and applicability for credit.

comment.en-US: May include articulation agreements, memoranda of understanding, or similar arrangements that govern how learning achievements are recognized across organizations or other boundaries.

description.en-US: Surrogate resource to which other resources are mapped in order to indicate their common transferability.

usageNote.en-US: Used when multiple resources such as courses are grouped together to indicate they have mutually agreed upon transfer value.

description.en-US: Description of learning value from one context when transferred to another.

comment.en-US: The learning value described in a Transfer Value Profile is commonly expressed as credit earned in one context and applied toward another, enabling a person to fulfill requirements without repeating equivalent learning. Other forms of recognition of prior learning, such as competencies or exemptions, may also be described.

usageNote.en-US: Transfer Value Profile is used to describe learning value in contexts such as recognition of prior learning or transfer. It does not describe the inherent credit value of a resource within the organization that owns or offers it; use ceterms:creditValue with a Value Profile for that purpose.

description.en-US: A description of value awarded for, required by, or otherwise related to the resource.

comment.en-US: Includes, but is not limited to, verification of whether quality assurance credentials have been issued for organizations, learning opportunities, and assessments.

Collection of tasks and competencies that embody a particular function in one or more jobs.

Monetary value or range.
A point value or interval for product characteristics and other purposes.

usageNote.en-US: Use in CTDL to describe quantitative values such as minimum and maximum credits or credit hours, etc.

usageNote.en-US: Punctuation accompanying alphanumeric strings should not be included.

usageNote.en-US: For assessments and rubrics, this can be used to indicate the scoring algorithm.

usageNote.en-US: Values may be just a year (e.g. 2026) or a year and a month (e.g. (2026-05).  If the full date, i.e. year, month and day, are known use ceterms:closingDate.

comment.en-US: The value should be in ISO 8601 date format; specifically YYYY or YYY-MM.

usageNote.en-US: Values may be just a year (e.g. 2026) or a year and a month (e.g. (2026-05).  If the full date, i.e. year, month and day, are known use ceterms:dateEffective.

comment.en-US: The duration will be specified using ISO8601 duration format. Common examples indicate that a salary is given on a per annum basis, in which case the value would be P1Y; for an hourly rate of pay the value would be PT1H.

usageNote.en-US: Values should be a full date, i.e. year, month and day; if the day or month are not known use ceterms:approximateClosingDate instead.

comment.en-US: Examples include course codes (e.g., "ENG101"), US Standard Occupation Codes (e.g., "31-9091"), North American Industry Classification System codes (e.g., "236117"), or any other bespoke code used by the provider of the resource to identify it.

usageNote.en-US: For identifiers that come from a recognized identification scheme use the specific property for that identifier type, such as ceterms:opeID, ceterms:ncesID, ceterms:leiCode, etc., or use ceterms:identifier so that the identification schema can be named.

For example, resources with type CredentialComponent may identify a specific subclass of ceterms:Credential; resources typed as a subclass of ceterms:Credential may identify a specific instance of ceterms:CredentialType.

description.en-US: The level of credit associated with the credit awarded or required.

A credit-related value.

Globally unique Credential Transparency Identifier (CTID) by which the creator, owner or provider of a resource recognizes it in transactions with the external environment (e.g., in verifiable claims involving the resource).

comment.en-US: The CTID is the equivalent of a version identifier for the resource. Different versions of a resource are considered distinct expressions and each must be assigned its own CTID. Each version of a resource can have only one CTID assigned. However, a single version of a resource may have distinct identifier values for both the ctid property and the credentialId property. In such a case both identifiers will be recognized by the resource creator/owner/provider in transactions with the external environment.

usageNote.en-US: Where possible, values should be taken from published frameworks defining degree majors, minors, and concentrations such as the U.S. National Center for Education Statistics' (NCES) Classification of Instructional Programs (CIP).

usageNote.en-US: Best practice is to use concepts from a controlled vocabulary such as the ceterms:DeliveryType vocabulary.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice for developing credential descriptions for the Credential Engine Registry is to use the ceterms:CostType vocabulary.

description.en-US: Dun & Bradstreet DUNS number for identifying an organization or business person.
Email address of the organization or person.
Date some event or activity ends.

usageNote.en-US: Values should be a full date, i.e. year, month and day; if the day or month are not known use ceterms:approximateEndDate instead.

description.en-US: Requirements for entry into a credentialing program, a learning opportunity, or an assessment, including credentials, transcripts, records of previous experience, or other forms of entry documentation.

usageNote.en-US: For Courses required to be taken before entry into another Course, use prerequisite.

description.en-US: Type of condition in the physical work performance environment that entails risk exposures requiring mitigating processes; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

comment.en-US: Such types may include exposure to bloodborne pathogens, airborne communicable diseases and dangerous chemicals, battlefield conditions, fire fighting, law enforcement, and so on.

description.en-US: Estimated cost of a credential, learning opportunity or assessment.
Estimated time it will take to complete an activity, event, or resource.
Summary of evidence about this resource.
Description of a process used to appraise this resource.
Entity that proves that the action occurred or that the action continues to be valid.

comment.en-US: The evidence verifies the information in the action and is particular to it. It is not a collection relating to several unrelated actions or a description of how such verifications might generically be characterized. It may comprise more than one evidentiary entity relating to the same action.

description.en-US: Relevant concepts in two entities being compared are coextensive.
Overall span of time it will take to complete the activity, event, or resource.

comment.en-US: This is intended to indicate overall time span, regardless of what portion of that time is spent actively pursuing the completion of the activity, event, or resource.

description.en-US: Amount and nature of required work, experiential learning or other relevant experience.
Date beyond which the resource is no longer offered or available.

comment.en-US: Previously earned, completed, or attained resources may still be valid even if they are no longer offered.

usageNote.en-US: Values should be a full date, i.e. year, month and day; if the day or month are not known use ceterms:approximateStartDate instead.

description.en-US: Types of external stakeholders that provide input to an entity's processes or resources; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice for developing credential descriptions for the Credential Engine Registry is to use the ceterms:ExternalInput vocabulary.

description.en-US: Research that supports or validates one or more aspects of the entity.
Description of a specific aspect or characteristic of this resource.

usageNote.en-US: Use for the level descriptors of a Qualifications Framework when these are defined in terms of several different types of competency.

Description of the amount of financial assistance available.
Date the organization was founded.

comment.en-US: This may define a place at any scale. Examples include a city, state, province, country, or continent.

usageNote.en-US: It is recommended to use services such as http://www.geonames.org to provide values for this property.

comment.en-US: Such partitive components can frequently be used in more than one context.

usageNote.en-US: Do not use this property if a simple text property such as ceterms:description is adequate.

comment.en-US: Examples include differentiating those progression levels or credential types that are relevant to different sectors, such as General Education, Higher Education and Technical / Vocational Education and Training.

description.en-US: Indicates the level of demand for a resource via a demand level action.
Work Role related to this resource.
Upper interquartile earnings.
Whether or not the credential holder must authorize the organization to provide the verification service.

usageNote.en-US: Where a specific property for the originating context or scheme exists, such as ceterms:opeID, ceterms:ncesID, ceterms:leiCode, etc., use that property instead of this one. Where the identifier has no nameable originating context or scheme other than that of the resource being identified, ceterms:codedNotation may be used.

description.en-US: Framework, scheme, type, or other organizing principle of this identifier.
Formal name or acronym of the framework, scheme, type, or other organizing principle of this identifier, such as ISBN or ISSN.
Alphanumeric string identifier of the entity.

comment.en-US: Where a formal identification system exists for the identifier, recommended best practice is to use a string conforming to that system.

description.en-US: Image, icon or logo that represents the entity including registered trade or service marks.

An inventory or listing of resources that includes this resource.
Assertion by an agent that this resource has a specific workforce demand level.
Category or class of credential that is typical for a level in a qualifications framework or similar progression model.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice in identifying industries for U.S. resources is to provide the NAICS code using the ceterms:naics property. Other resources may use the ceterms:industrytype property and any framework of the class ceterms:IndustryClassification.

description.en-US: The primary language or languages of the entity, even if it makes use of other languages.

usageNote.en-US: A course offered in English to teach Spanish would have an inLanguage of English, while a credential in Quebec could have an inLanguage of both French and English.

description.en-US: Indicates a Qualifications Framework that uses this resource.
Type of instructional program; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

usageNote.en-US: For U.S. credentials, best practice is to use a framework such as the CIP (Classification of Instructional Programs). Other credentials may use any framework of the class CTDL InstructionalProgramClassification.

description.en-US: Resource used to carry out an action or process.

comment.en-US: May be a credential or rubric whose criteria were applied in executing the action or process; may be a data set profile that provided measurements of relevant metrics.

usageNote.en-US: A third-party credential agent claiming that its credential provides advanced standing for the credential of another credential agent should consider using ceterms:recommendedFor instead of ceterms:advancedStandingFor in the absence of an explicit and verifiable agreement on advanced standing between the agents of the two credentials.

comment.en-US: The ceterms:jurisdictionalException property is used in conjunction with the ceterms:jurisdiction property and expresses any exceptions to a more general statement; e.g., the United states except for Colorado.

description.en-US: Keyword or key phrase describing relevant aspects of an entity.

usageNote.en-US: Use the keyword property to enter free text keywords. A subject concept in a controlled vocabulary should use the subject property.

usageNote.en-US: "Framework" may be interpreted broadly to include any scheme or schema for organizing and referencing resources.

description.en-US: Primary academic discipline or professional career path.

comment.en-US: May be useful for describing credentials, assessments and learning opportunities that cover a general field but with a focus on a specific skill set, for example an apprenticeship in electrical engineering specializing in High Voltage applications. For degree credentials there are also properties for degree major, minor and concentration.

usageNote.en-US: Normally there will be only one specialist subject; to indicate the general topicality of a resource use ceterms:subject.

description.en-US: Date the validity or usefulness of the information in this resource begins.

usageNote.en-US: Values should be a full date, i.e. year, month and day; if the day or month are not known use ceterms:approximateStartDate instead.

description.en-US: Verbatim unformatted text of a statement, typically one made in a larger document.

usageNote.en-US: Use ceterms:description if the data provided is a summary of the content, e.g. when linking to the statement.

description.en-US: Indicates the topic or nature of the statement within the context of the document being represented.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice is to draw from an existing concept scheme such as ceterms:StatementCategory, which may be supplemented by more precise terms from a locally defined concept scheme if required.

description.en-US: Street address. e.g. "1600 Amphitheatre Pkwy".
Indicates a broader type or class than the one being described.

comment.en-US: Similar to rdfs:subClassOf, this property means that all examples of the type of resource being described are also instances of the class indicated, however it does not imply that the subject is an rdfs:Class.

usageNote.en-US: Used in CTDL to indicate the Credential Class (i.e. subclass of ceterms:Credential) that encompasses this type of credential.

description.en-US: Words or brief phrases describing the topicality of the entity; select subject terms from an existing enumeration of such terms.

usageNote.en-US: Use the subject property to reference a concept in a controlled vocabulary. Free text subjects should use the keyword property.

description.en-US: Webpage that describes this entity.

comment.en-US: The web page being referenced describes the entity. The value of subjectWebpage is an authoritative location for information about the subject but should not be assumed to be a persistent identifier of the subject.

description.en-US: Artifact to be submitted such as a transcript, portfolio, or an affidavit.
Name, label, or description of an artifact to be submitted such as a transcript, portfolio, or an affidavit.
Organization in a subordinate or lower position than a parent organization.
An administrative subdivision within a country that is intermediate between a region and a locality.

comment.en-US: This may be referred to as a county in the United States, a département in France, a district in India, a raion in Russia, a municipio in Mexico, or equivalent terms in other jurisdictions.

description.en-US: Resource that replaces this resource.

comment.en-US: For example, a credential that outright replaces the credential being described, and is not simply a newer version of the same credential (the two credentials have different CTIDs).

description.en-US: Resource that this resource replaces.

comment.en-US: For example, the credential that is outright replaced by the credential being described, and is not simply an older version of the same credential (the two credentials have different CTIDs).

description.en-US: Requirements to qualify for  a support service.
Resource to which this support service is applicable.
Webpage or online document that defines or explains the nature of support services offered by the organization.
Description of the nature of support services offered by the organization.
Types of support services offered by an agent; select from an existing enumeration of such types.
Assessment that provides direct, indirect, formative or summative evaluation or estimation of the nature, ability, or quality for an entity.
A competency relevant to the resource being described.
Competency framework relevant to the process being described.
Resource that targets this Competency for a particular purpose.
Candidate PathwayComponent for the ComponentCondition.
Options for contacting the organization or person.
Credential that is a focus or target of the condition, process or verification service.
Job that is the focus or target of this resource.
Learning opportunity that is the focus of a condition, process or another learning opportunity.
Learning object or resource that is used as part of a learning activity.

comment.en-US: Examples include a textbook or lesson plan that describes or records the educational activity (e.g. an audio- or video-recording of a lesson).

description.en-US: Metric used to assess whether a condition has been met.
Individual entry in a formally defined framework that is the target of an alignment.

comment.en-US: The target node returned must be the exact competency or concept being described and no other competency or concept. References to data or a document that returns all of the competencies or concepts in the framework to which the target node belongs should use the ceterms:framework property.

usageNote.en-US: "Framework" may be interpreted broadly to include any scheme or schema for organizing and referencing resources.

description.en-US: Textual description of an individual entry in a formally defined framework that is the target of an alignment.

usageNote.en-US: "Framework" may be interpreted broadly to include any scheme or schema for organizing and referencing resources.

description.en-US: Name of an individual entry in a formally defined framework that is the target of an alignment.

usageNote.en-US: "Framework" may be interpreted broadly to include any scheme or schema for organizing and referencing resources.

description.en-US: Occupation that is the focus or target of this resource.
Pathway in which this resource is a potential component.
Task that is the focus or target of this resource.
Competency that the learning opportunity is intended to teach.
Telephone number.
Total engaged or participating time it will take to complete the activity, event, or resource.

comment.en-US: This is intended to indicate only the sum of the individual amounts of time which are spent actively engaged in pursuing the completion of the activity, event, or resource, regardless of the overall time span required to complete it.

usageNote.en-US: If a resource takes 50 hours over a span of 6 months to complete, use this to record 50 hours as PT50H.

description.en-US: Value that may be transferred.

comment.en-US: For example, this may be the credit value earned in one context that may be applied to another, but other forms of recognition of prior learning are also relevant.

description.en-US: Resource for which the described transfer value is applicable.

comment.en-US: When this property references multiple resources, those resources should be treated as a set for which, collectively, the transfer value is applicable.

description.en-US: Resource from which the described transfer value originates.

comment.en-US: When this property references multiple resources, those resources should be treated as a set from which, collectively, the transfer value originates.

description.en-US: Webpage or online document that defines or explains the nature of transfer value handled by the organization.
Description of the nature of transfer value handled by the organization.
Reference to a service that is used to verify this Credential or type of credential.
Directory of credential holders and their current statuses.
Textual description of the methods used to evaluate an assessment, learning opportunity, process or verificaiton service for validity or reliability.
Direct access to the verification service.

comment.en-US: This property identifies machine-accessible services, such as API endpoints, that provide direct access to the verification service being described.

usageNote.en-US: For general webpages describing the service, use the subjectWebpage property.

description.en-US: Type of claim provided through a verification service; select from an existing enumeration of such types.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice for developing credential descriptions for the Credential Engine Registry is to use the ceterms:ClaimType vocabulary.

description.en-US: Alphanumeric identifier of the version of the resource that is unique within the organizational context of its owner and which does not need the context of other information in order to be interpreted.

usageNote.en-US: Intended for simple string and/or numeric version codes or identifiers, such as "10" or "3B.1" or "2024 Release". For version identifiers that need to reference additional information, such as a type of version or framework for versioning, use versionIdentifier.

description.en-US: Alphanumeric identifier of the version of the resource and information about the identifier's originating context or scheme.

usageNote.en-US: Use versionCode for any local identifier of the version of the resource that come from the organizational context its owner and which do not need the context of other information in order to be interpreted.

description.en-US: Measurement of the weight, degree, percent, or strength of a recommendation, requirement, or comparison.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice is to assign a decimal value weight between 0 and 1 that indicates the strength of the assertion, with 0 being weakest and 1 being strongest.

description.en-US: Monetary compensation associated with work.
Years of relevant experience.

usageNote.en-US: Non-integer year values may be expressed as point value, for example, 0.25, 1.5, etc.

description.en-US: Further information about an object or topic supplied as free text.
The format of the note.
The textual content of further information about an object or topic supplied as free text.
Links an individual to an individual; such an owl:sameAs statement indicates that two URI references actually refer to the same thing: the individuals have the same "identity".
Type of method by which the data was collected.
Credentialing organization or a third party providing the data.
Quotient of two values of the data set, expressed as a percentage.

usageNote.en-US: Best practice is to treat the value of this property as a verbatim percentage; for example, a value of 1.5 should be interpreted as 1.5%

description.en-US: Data Set on which earnings or employment data is based.
A description of the item.
The upper value of some characteristic or property.

usageNote.en-US: In CTDL: for single values, use schema:value; for ranges, use schema:minValue and schema:maxValue.

description.en-US: The lower value of some characteristic or property.

usageNote.en-US: In CTDL: for single values, use schema:value; for ranges, use schema:minValue and schema:maxValue.

description.en-US: A CreativeWork or Event about this Thing.
A string or text indicating the unit of measurement.
The value of the property value node.

usageNote.en-US: In CTDL: for single values, use schema:value; for ranges, use schema:minValue and schema:maxValue.
